name: Service worker request interception
plain: A service worker sits between the page and the network and can answer any request itself.
meaning: Once registered, it sees the URL of every request in its scope, can rewrite or fake responses and can serve pages offline. The Service-Worker-Allowed header widens that scope to the whole origin.

web.api: addEventListener('fetch', e => e.respondWith(…)); Service-Worker-Allowed header; navigation preload; static routing API

access.prompt_ui: None for registration. Secure context required

data.metric: A service worker sits between the page and the network and can answer any request itself.

limits.headline: Can answer or change every request the site makes, on every browser
limits.user_action: None, the page reads it silently
can: See each in scope request URL
Control the whole origin when the header allows it
cannot: See requests of other origins outside its scope
Run on a page outside a secure context
limits.differs: All six browsers support it. Static routing is missing in Safari and iPhone.

story.what_it_is: A small script that stays installed and can intercept the site's own network traffic.

marketing.name: Service Worker API
marketing.pitch: Lets a site control caching and offline behavior.

story.for_you: Sites load faster and work offline. The same hook is also a place for code to live between visits.
story.for_makers: Makers rely on it for offline apps, caching and push.

use_cases.example: A news site serves cached stories when the train goes into a tunnel.

risks: A persistence point for first party code
Sees every in scope request URL

technical_bounds: Scope limited unless Service-Worker-Allowed widens it

abuse: A persistence point for tracking code
